'''''Leucospermum patersonii''''' is a large [[evergreen]], upright shrub of up to {{convert|4|m|ft|abbr=on}} high that is assigned to the family [[Proteaceae]]. It has large, roundish hairless leaves with three to eight teeths and egg- to globe-shaped, orange flower heads of {{convert|8|–|9|cm|in|abbr=on}} across. From the center of each flower emerges a long orange style with a thickened tip that is bent to the center of the head, giving the entire head the appearance of a pincushion. It is called '''silveredge pincushion''' in English. Flowers can be found between August and December. It is an [[Endemism|endemic species]] limited to the south coast of the [[Western Cape]] province of South Africa.<ref name=Rourke />

== Description ==
The silveredge pincushion is a large, rounded shrub or sometimes a small tree of up to {{convert|4|m|ft|abbr=on}} high, that has a stout trunk of {{convert|10|–|20|cm|in|round=0.5|abbr=on}} in diameter covered in a thick corky bark. The flowering stems are upright, woody, {{convert|8|–|10|mm|in|abbr=on}} in diameter, densely covered in short fine cringy hairs and some straight, spreading hairs. The hairless leaves are almost round to rounded rectangular, {{convert|5|–|9|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|3|–|5|cm|in|abbr=on}} wide, [[Glossary of leaf morphology#cordate|hart-shaped]] foot or with [[Glossary of leaf morphology#auriculate|ears]] reaching beyond the stem and a rounded tip with three to eight, deep, bony teeth, are set alternately, directed at an upward angle, overlapping, crowded near the branch tips.<ref name=Rourke /><ref name=PZA>{{cite web|website= SANBI PlantZAfrica.com|title= Leucospermum patersonii|url= http://pza.sanbi.org/leucospermum-patersonii}}</ref>

The flower heads are egg- to globe-shaped, about {{convert|8|–|9|cm|in|abbr=on}} across, usually set individually but occasionally clustered with two or three together, each set on a [[Peduncle (botany)|stalk]] {{convert|1|–|2|cm|in|abbr=on}} long. The [[Receptacle (botany)|common base]] of the flowers in the same head is narrowly cone-shaped with a pointy tip, {{convert|4|–|5|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|7|–|10|mm|in|abbr=on}} wide. The [[Bract#Involucral bracts|bracts]] subtending the flower head are pointy oval in shape, about {{convert|10|mm|in|abbr=on}} long an {{convert|7|mm|in|abbr=on}} wide, tightly pressed and overlapping, cartilaginous in consistency and finely powdery hairy or hairless.<ref name=Rourke />

The [[Bracteole|bracts]] at the base of the individual flower is inverted egg-shaped, convex and keeled, with a pointy tip, densely woolly neat the foot, about {{convert|10|mm|in|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|8|mm|in|abbr=on}} wide. The [[Merosity|4-merous]] [[perianth]] is {{convert|2+1/2|–|3|cm|in|abbr=on}} long, very strongly curved towards the center of the head in the bud, and orange to crimson in colour. In the lower part, where the lobes remain merged when the flower has opened (called tube), the lobes are tapering, about {{convert|5|mm|in|abbr=on}} long, cylinder-shaped and hairless. The lobes in the middle part (or [[Petal#Shape and size|claws]]), where the perianth is split lengthwise, curve back on their base when the flower opens, and is densely woolly hairy. The upper part, which enclosed the pollen presenter in the bud consists of four strongly recurved, oval [[Petal#Shape an size|limbs]] of about {{convert|4|mm|in|abbr=on}} long, hairless of {{clarify|date=December 2021}} with some stiff, bristly hairs. From the perianth emerges a [[Stigma (botany)#Style|style]] of {{convert|4+1/2|–|5|cm|in|abbr=on}} long, strongly bent towards the center of the head. The so-called [[pollen presenter]], onto which the pollen is transferred from the anthers in the bud, is shaped like a skewed spinning top, {{convert|3|–|4|mm|in|abbr=on}} long and about {{convert|2|mm|in|abbr=on}} in diameter, with an oblique groove that performs the function of the stigma across the very tip. The [[Ovary (botany)|ovary]] is subtended by four awl-shaped pale orange scales of about {{convert|4|mm|in|abbr=on}} long.<ref name=Rourke />

=== Differences with related species ===
The silveredge pincushion differs from its relatives by the tree-like habit (shared with ''L. conocarpodendron''), large, roundish leaves with three to eight teeths, the middle part of the flower woolly hairy, and the skewed, spinning-top shaped pollen presenter.<ref name=Rourke />

== Taxonomy ==
The silveredge pincushion had been collected by some of the earliest [[Plant collecting|plant collectors]], among which excellent specimens collected by Oldenland, who was master gardener in service of the [[Dutch East India Company]] at the Cape up until the year 1697. [[Johannes Burman]] and [[Johann Christian Daniel von Schreber|J.C.D. von Schreber]] had these specimens in their [[herbarium]] collections, but filed them as ''[[Leucospermum conocarpodendron|L. conocarpodendron]]'', and their distinctiveness was overlooked for over two hundred years. After it was collected again in 1922 by a Mr. H.W. Paterson who, lived in [[Hermanus]], it was scientifically described for the first time by [[Edwin Percy Phillips|Phillips]] in 1928. He named it ''Leucospermum patersonii'', in the collector's honor. No other scientific names for this species exist.<ref name=Rourke />

''L. patersonii'' has been assigned to the showy pincushions, section ''[[Leucospermum#Brevifilamentum|Brevifilamentum]]''.<ref name=PAP>{{cite web|website= Protea Atlas Project|title= Fireworks pincushions|url= https://www.proteaatlas.org.za/pincush4.htm}}</ref>

== Distribution, habitat and ecology ==
''L. patersonii'' can be found between [[Cape Agulhas]] in the east along the coast to [[Stanford, Western Cape|Stanford]], with an outlying population at Heuningklip Kloof, near [[Kleinmond]]. It also used to occur near [[Hermanus]] but went extinct there. The silveredge pincushion is a species of the coast that is almost restricted to limestone ridges next to the sea between {{convert|50|and|250|m|ft|abbr=on}} altitudes. Except for the population at Heuningklip Kloof, the species grows on limestone of the [[Alexandria Formation]]. In roots mostly penetrating the system soft layers of limestone closer to the surface. The silveredge pincushion usually grows in fairly dense stands in a vegetation that also contains other Proteaceae with a preference for limestone, including ''[[Mimetes saxatilis]]'', ''[[Protea obtusifolia]]'' and ''[[Leucadendron meridianum]]''. Mature plants are able to regenerate from the tips of the branches, if the [[wildfire]]s that periodically occur in the [[fynbos]] are not too hot.<ref name=Rourke />

== Cultivation ==
The upright habit and large conspicuous flower heads make ''L. patersonii'' attractive as a cut flower and ornamental species. Because it is adapted to lime, it is used to make hybrids that can grow on a range of soil types. Several such hybrids have been developed by crossing ''L. patersonii'' with ''L. conocarpodendron'', which is itself intolerant of lime.<ref>{{cite journal|first1= Y.|last1= Shchori|first2= J.|last2= Ben-Jaacov|first3= A.|last3= Ackerman|first4= S.|last4= Gilad|first5= B.|last5= Metchnik|year= 1995|title= Horticultural Characters of Intraspecific Hybrids of ''Leucospermum patersonii'' × ''Leucospermum conocarpodendron''|journal= Acta Horticulturae|volume= 420|pages= 135–137|url= https://www.ishs.org/ishs-article/420_37}}</ref>
